script.text: Far away, where the rainbows go to rest, there is a magical place called Rainbow Forest.
And every single morning there begins with the same sweet sound.
That bell belongs to Glitter. And the little one bouncing along behind her — that is Princess.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Hi, friend! We're going somewhere very special today. Would you like to come with us?
Princess did not know it yet. But this would be a morning she would never, ever forget.
They walked together under enormous flowers and curling rainbow vines.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Stay close enough to hear my bell, little one.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: I love your bell, Mama. It sounds like tiny stars laughing.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: And if we are ever apart, you remember what to do.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Stop. Take a breath. And listen.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Then call for me, and wait somewhere safe.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: And if I still can't find you?

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Then go to the last safe place we both remember. And I will always, always come looking for you.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: (singing) Stay near my bell, stay close on your way… if the forest grows quiet — stop, listen, and stay.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Will your bell always bring me home?

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: My bell. Your courage. And a little help from your friends.
Their special place was called Moonwater Spring — where the water shimmers with a little piece of the night sky, even in the morning.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Mmm! It tastes like starlight!

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: With just a sprinkle of moonbeam, I think.
And from that spring, glowing water runs out through the roots of the forest, to every flower and every tree and every creature in it.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Does the whole forest need it?

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Every single drop.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Then I hope it never, ever stops flowing.
But on the way home, from behind a curtain of silver vines, came the smallest sound.

script.speaker: Fireflies
script.text: Help! Please, help us!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Mama, wait! Somebody needs us!

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: I'm right here. Stay where you can hear my bell.
A whole family of fireflies was tangled in the sticky vines, their little lights blinking on and off.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Don't be frightened, little lights. I'll get you out.
Princess lifted the vines with her horn — carefully, carefully — until every last firefly wriggled free.

script.speaker: Fireflies
script.text: We're free! Thank you, Princess!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Helping somebody makes my heart feel warm.
And then the wind came. Thick golden fog came tumbling between the trees, and a heavy branch crashed down across the path — right between Princess and her mother.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Princess! Stay where you are! I'm coming!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Mama!
But the wind was loud. And her mother's voice, and her mother's bell, were somewhere on the other side of it.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Mama?
Princess started to run — and then she stopped herself.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: No. Running could take me even further away.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Stop. Take a breath. And listen.
So she did. She stood very still in the fog, and she listened with her whole heart.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Can you hear her bell, friend?
But there was no ring, ring, ring. There was nothing at all.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: I think… I think I'm lost.
And that is a very big feeling, for somebody very small.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: But I remember the rest of what Mama taught me. If I can't find her by myself… I can ask for help.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: Chirp! Who are you calling for?
A small blue bird hopped out of the fog.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: My mama. Her name is Glitter. She has a rainbow mane, and a silver bell.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: I'm Pip! And I know nearly every path in Rainbow Forest.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: …Nearly?

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: Well. The ones that aren't covered in fog. But cheer up — two heads are better than one. And four eyes are better than two!
Then Pip spotted something in the soft mud: hoofprints.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: Unicorn tracks!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Mama's hoofprints! Let's follow them. Together?

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: Together.
The tracks led them to a narrow rope bridge, swaying over a rushing stream.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: That bridge looks very wobbly.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: It also looks very creaky.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: …Extremely creaky.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Step by step. Slow and steady.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: Please don't step on my tail!
Out from under the bridge came a small green dragon, shaking from his nose to the end of his tail.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: I'm Moss. I wanted to cross, but I'm afraid of heights. And deep water. And bridges. Especially bridges.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Hello, Moss. Have you seen a big unicorn with a rainbow mane?

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: No. But I'll help you look.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Being brave doesn't mean you're not scared, Moss. It means you keep going, even when you are.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: Then… perhaps I can be brave for one bridge.
On the other side lay a whole field of enormous, glowing mushrooms.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: How do we ever get across?
Princess put one hoof on a mushroom — and it bent, and it bounced, and up she went!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Wheeee!

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: The forest has given us a shortcut!

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: Or a very bouncy mistake.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: I'm flying! …Sort of!
And for one small moment, in the middle of a very frightening day, all three of them laughed out loud.
Then the clouds rolled over the sun, and the rain came down — and washed every one of those hoofprints away.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: No! Mama's tracks!

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: I don't like storms.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Stay close to me, Moss. We'll face it together.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: But how will we ever find your mama now?
And Princess stood very still in the rain, and remembered.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Mama said: go to the last safe place we both remember.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: Moonwater Spring!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: That's where she'll come looking. Let's go!
And far away, through the very same rain, Glitter was running and calling.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Princess! Princess, where are you?
Until her silver bell caught fast on a thorny branch — and the strap snapped, and the bell fell silently into the wet grass.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Oh no. My bell!
And now there was no ringing left in the forest at all.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Moonwater Spring. Princess will remember. She will remember.
When the three friends reached the clearing at last, something was terribly wrong.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: The spring! It's… it's gone dark.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: Where has all the water gone?
They followed a thin little trickle of water, all the way to a crack in the rocks — and a dark, quiet cave.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: In there. That's where the water is going.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: It is very dark in there.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Then we shouldn't go in without a plan… wait. Little lights! Are you there?

script.speaker: Fireflies
script.text: Follow us!
And out of the trees came the fireflies Princess had saved that very morning — and they made a glowing golden trail, right into the dark.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Moss, stay close to me. Pip, watch the way behind us.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: I'm still afraid.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: So am I. We can be afraid and brave at the same time.
Deep inside the cave, an enormous crystal had fallen right across the underground river. The water pushed and pushed behind it — and could not get through.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: We have to move it. Push!
She pushed with all her might. It did not move. Not even a little.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: It's too heavy.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: Not if we all work together! I'll pull!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: I'll push from below. Moss — we need somebody at the top.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: But I can't fly.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: You flew over the mushrooms.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: I floated. Very briefly!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: You don't have to fly far. Just one brave flap at a time.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: One brave flap at a time…
And Moss flapped once. And twice. And up he went!

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: I'm flying! I'm really flying!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Ready? One, two, three — PUSH!
Princess pushed. Pip pulled. Moss shoved from the very top. And the great crystal rolled aside — and the water burst free, bright and glowing, rushing out into the forest.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Wait. Listen!

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: (far away) Princess!

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Mama!
Moonwater Spring came back to life, shining like the moon come home — and that light spilled out through the trees, all the way to a mother searching in the rain.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Princess!
And Princess ran faster than she had ever run in her whole life.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Oh, my brave girl. I was so worried.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: I was worried too, Mama. But I stopped. And I breathed. And I listened. And I asked for help. And then I came to our safe place.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: You remembered every single thing.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: And Pip and Moss helped me. We saved the spring together!

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: Three heads really are better than one.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: And I flew!

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: …Sort of.

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: I definitely flew.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Princess — I have something for you.
And from beneath her mane, Glitter lifted a tiny silver bell, just Princess's size.

script.speaker: Glitter
script.text: Not because you will never be lost again. But because now you know exactly what to do when the way feels uncertain.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Ring, ring, ring! It sounds just like yours!

script.speaker: Moss
script.text: Only smaller.

script.speaker: Pip
script.text: And much more bouncy.
And so that was the day Princess got lost in the fog — and found her own way home again.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: Friend? I learned something today. When you can't find somebody you love — you don't run. You stop. You take a breath. And you listen.

script.speaker: Princess
script.text: And then you go to the place you both know. And if you feel too small… you ask a friend. Two heads really are better than one.
And as the evening came down over Rainbow Forest, two silver bells rang together — one big, and one small.
